items.title: feat(pm-stack): rung-4 watchdog escalation hand-off (#6033)
items.body: Implements the rung-4 escalation hand-off for the quota watchdog (issue #6033, design #6031). The decision layer (#6032, `pm-stack/exporters/src/watchdog-state.ts`) already decides `escalate` once every rung is spent; this PR adds the effect layer that word stands for, behind injected effectors so the policy is fully testable without a queue, network, or browser — the same layering #6032 used. ## What lands - `src/watchdog-escalation.ts` - `buildEscalationPacket` — the full context packet from #6033: outcome wanted (source produces a fresh `latest.json` with real quota windows), failure context (class, consecutive failures, the persisted `repairLog`, producer history reference, state-file path, adapter reference), required capability (browser-enabled agent; laptop Helium via CDP :19222; adapter origins only), acceptance (fresh producer document lands; the watchdog auto-closes), and the stop conditions (human-only challenge → mark human-blocked; outside the origin allowlist → stop and report on the incident issue). - `planEscalation` — exactly one `enqueue_task` + one `open_issue` for an escalating incident; returns `deduped: true` and no actions when the incident already carries an escalation record for the same (source, class) pair. - `recordEscalation` — persists the confirmed queue task id / issue number onto the incident. - `planRecovery` — on producer success: comment the resolution, close the incident issue, complete the queue task (state-side, `decide`'s healthy path clears the incident in the same tick). - `surfacingLine` — the NEEDS DREW line: immediate (same tick) when human-blocked with a one-line reason; for ordinary escalations only after 24 h unresolved (`ESCALATION_NEEDS_DREW_AFTER_MS`), quiet before that. - `applyEscalationActions` — runs planned actions through the injected effectors in order. - `src/watchdog-state.ts` — `Incident` gains an optional `escalation` record (`EscalationRecord`); `coerceHealth` validates it structurally and drops malformed records, so older state files keep reading cleanly. - `test/watchdog-escalation.test.ts` — one test per #6033 acceptance criterion (dedup, packet completeness, recovery sequence, human-blocked same-tick surfacing, 24 h quiet period, coercion round-trip), oracle = the acceptance text. - README updated: the rung-4 module is no longer listed as missing. ## Tests `bun test ../exporters/test/watchdog-escalation.test.ts ../exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts` from pm-stack/aggregator: **21 pass, 0 fail** (includes the existing #6032 PBT/MBT suites — no regressions). ## Remaining (owned by the #6032 remainder, noted in the README) The oneshot entry point (`src/watchdog.ts` in exporters) that reads state, calls `decide`, and wires the production effectors (fleet CLI enqueue, gh issue create/comment/close) to these planners. This PR deliberately does not invent that host. Links: task 14781 · issue #6033 · design #6031 · core #6032 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(pm-stack): quota watchdog core — entry point, adapters, rung executors, systemd timer (#6032)
items.body: ## What this builds (#6032 remainder) Slice 1 (decision layer, PR #7788) and rung 4 (escalation, PR #8357) already landed. This PR builds the rest of the watchdog core: - **`src/watchdog.ts`** — the oneshot entry point. Per tick: load adapters, read the state file through `coerceHealth`, observe each source (producer document + gatherer heartbeat + live CDP liveness probe), classify (including missing-document, stale-read-while-the-browser-lives, and dead-CDP — the classes the producer cannot see itself), `decide`, execute the rung, run rung-4 escalation/recovery, write state back atomically (tmp+rename), append `quota-watchdog-history.jsonl`. Nothing decision-relevant lives in process memory (#5928). - **Rung executors** — rung 2: CDP re-validation (`/json/version` + `/json/list`, allowlist origin open, cookies present **by name** via the CDP websocket — values never enter the process) with one bounded supervised restart of the adapter's browser unit; rung 3: re-login driver that stops dead at a human-only challenge and marks the incident human-blocked. Repairs are gated on `QUOTA_WATCHDOG_LIVE_REPAIRS=1`, rung-4 production effectors (fleet queue / `gh`) on `QUOTA_WATCHDOG_LIVE=1`; the systemd unit sets both, a bare CLI run journals dry-run plans and creates nothing. - **`src/adapters.ts` + `adapters/fixture.json`** — the adapter loader: per-provider JSON (origins allowlist, CDP port, data paths, cookie names, login hints, class/rung maps, thresholds), structurally validated, defects reported per file instead of throwing. The core contains zero provider names; the fixture adapter is the one shipped here, real provider adapters are follow-ons per the issue scope. - **`producers/producer-template.mjs`** — forkable producer scaffold from the retired Meta producer pattern (timeout-bounded CDP, tab ownership, failure-class exit codes + failure documents, atomic `latest.json`), plus `test/fixtures/fixture-producer.mjs`, the scenario-driven stub the acceptance tests drive. - **`pm-stack/systemd/pm-quota-watchdog.{service,timer}`** — oneshot + timer on the gatherer cadence, offset to `*:3/15`. ## Tests (oracles named per the testing doctrine) `bun test ../exporters/test/` — **35 pass, 0 fail** (includes the pre-existing state + escalation suites). The new `test/watchdog.test.ts` drives the entry point end to end against a scratch tree: - broken source walks retry → CDP re-validation → re-login → escalation, caps honored (no rung >2× per incident), escalates exactly once and dedupes on later ticks; - rate-limited fixture sets `cooldownUntil` on disk and a fresh tick honors it with no repair action (the #5928 regression shape); - human-only challenge fixture marks the incident human-blocked with the surfacing flag and a same-tick NEEDS DREW line, and the ladder stops dead; - healthy source is quiet (state + history only, no output); - recovery after escalation comments/closes/completes the hand-off; - cross-invocation persistence: every tick re-reads state from disk. CLI fixture demo also run live: healthy tick quiet; `session-expired` scenario classified and rung 3 recorded (as `skipped` with live repairs off). Live install (units + timer + a laptop-local adapter for the Meta file-export source) and the ≥3-consecutive-tick demonstration follow the merge and are reported on #6032. items.body: Slice 1 of #6032 (design #6031). This lands the **pure decision layer** of the generic browser-dependent quota watchdog — the part the issue calls out as the natural fit for PBT/MBT — and leaves the I/O, browser and deployment shell to a follow-up with the boundary written down. ## What lands `pm-stack/exporters/src/watchdog-state.ts` - **Failure classes** — `session-expired`, `cookie-missing`, `endpoint-changed`, `browser-down`, `cdp-unreachable`, `rate-limited`, `unknown`, and the single place a class maps to a repair rung. - **Repair ladder** — `decide()` returns the next action (`quiet`, `wait-cooldown`, `retry`, `repair rung N`, `human-blocked`, `escalate`) plus the next persisted record. Per-rung attempts are capped at 2 per incident; a rate-limited source sets `cooldownUntil` on disk and the next tick honors it with no browser action; a rate limit whose cooldown rung is spent escalates rather than climbing to a browser repair. - **Disk state** — `SourceHealth` carries `lastAttemptAt`, `lastSuccessAt`, `consecutiveFailures`, `currentClass`, sanitized `lastDetail`, `cooldownUntil`, per-rung `rungAttempts`, a bounded (20) `repairLog`, and the incident identity + surfacing flag. `coerceHealth` reads a file back without trusting it: garbage yields a fresh record, never a throw and never an assumed-healthy. - **Sanitization** — credential-shaped text is redacted before it can reach the state file or a log. No I/O, no browser, no secrets, no provider names — the core is provider-agnostic by construction, which is what the adapter-loader criterion asks for. ## Tests name their oracles `pm-stack/exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts` — **12 pass, 0 fail**: - **PBT invariants** over generated tick sequences: per-rung attempts never exceed the cap; the repair log stays bounded; `consecutiveFailures` is monotonic while failing and resets on success; a healthy tick always clears the incident and is quiet; no secret-shaped value survives sanitization. - **MBT** — a reference model of the ladder written independently of the implementation, stepped in lockstep over 300 generated sequences; any divergence in action, rung, or failure count fails. - **Acceptance fixtures**: the broken-source walk (retry → CDP re-validation → re-login → escalation), the rate-limited cooldown persisted and honored then escalating, the human-only challenge marking the incident `human-blocked` with the surfacing flag and not re-hammering, and the healthy source staying quiet. ```bash cd pm-stack/aggregator && bun test ../exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts ``` Typecheck of both new files is clean under the repo's strict settings. ## What remains for #6032 (listed in `pm-stack/exporters/README.md`) The oneshot entry point (state read/write, `latest.json` + heartbeat reads, history append), the adapter loader and `adapters/`, the rung 2/3 executors, the rung-4 hand-off to #6033, producer scaffolding, and the systemd oneshot + timer. The issue stays open for those. Refs #6032, #6031. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

### Tokio broadcast channel calls clone in parallel, but does not require `Sync`
[GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The broadcast channel internally calls `clone` on the stored value when receiving it, and only requires `T:Send`. This means that using the broadcast channel with values that are `Send` but not `Sync` can trigger unsoundness if the `clone` implementation makes use of the value being `!Sync`.

Thank you to Austin Bonander for finding and reporting this issue.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 2.7 / 10 (Low)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U`
